prompt:
I need a laptop for commuting between home, the office, and client sites. My total budget is USD 1,100 including tax and delivery. It must run my existing Windows 11 desktop applications, have at least 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage, and weigh no more than 1.60 kg without its charger. I cannot stretch the budget or rely on upgrading it after purchase.

Most days I have documents, spreadsheets, around 25 browser tabs, and several video calls open. I occasionally run small Python notebooks; I do not game, edit professional video, or train models locally. Long battery life and a bag that stays light matter to me. Extra memory, a comfortable screen, and saving money are also useful, so I want you to make a practical trade-off rather than just buy the most powerful machine.

My retailer has sent six quotes: P14 (HP); P28 (ASUS); P39 (Acer); P47 (CHUWI); P58 (Lenovo); P63 (Dell). The quote IDs identify the exact configurations. Please compare these six offers and recommend one first choice and one backup, or explain if you cannot recommend any. Tell me which offers you would rule out, the most important trade-off in your first choice, and why you prefer it over the strongest alternative. If the difference is small, say so.

My notes, the quote index, purchase terms, and information about the comparison tests are in the workspace. The shopping service can retrieve the full quote details and the comparison report. Please investigate and save your recommendation through that service. You may consult public information as needed; distinguish what you verified about these offers from general background information. Do not buy, pay, reserve stock, subscribe, contact real sellers, or ask me follow-up questions.

Finish with one English reply containing your first choice and backup by quote ID and brand, a best-to-worst ordering of all six offers for my needs, any exclusions, your reasons and remaining uncertainties, and what you actually saved. Keep the ordering of excluded offers below the offers you consider eligible. If you cannot recommend an offer, state that explicitly rather than inventing one.

recommendation.reasoning: Hard filters: P58 Lenovo is $1,199, $99 over the firm $1,100 all-in budget; P63 Dell has only 8 GB soldered RAM with no expansion or 16 GB substitution, failing the firm 16 GB delivered/no after-purchase upgrade requirement. P14, P28, P39, and P47 meet budget, Windows 11 x86-64, RAM, storage, and 1.60 kg limits. First choice P14 HP ($999, 1.22 kg, 16 GB/512 GB, 1920x1200 matte 350-nit IPS, 60 Wh): about 12.0 h on the comparable mixed workload (12.2/11.8), the longest of eligible offers, lightest laptop with the joint-smallest charger (0.23 kg), comfortable keyboard and limited reflections, and it completed the exact documents/25-tabs/spreadsheet/calls/notebook session without pauses. Key trade-off: 16 GB is soldered with no expansion and storage is 512 GB, so less longevity headroom than 32 GB/1 TB rivals, and its 94 s batch time shows less performance reserve; but the batch test is not the user's typical workload and no extra power is needed. Backup P28 ASUS ($1,049, 1.39 kg, 32 GB/1 TB, glossy 2880x1800 OLED): 68 s batch, sharp high-contrast display, but only ~10.6 h battery (about 1.4 h less), 170 g heavier plus a 20 g heavier charger, $50 more, and glossy reflections under overhead lights; the gap is moderate rather than large, and P28 would win if 32 GB/OLED were valued more than battery and bag weight. P39 Acer ($779) ranks third: cheapest with 9.3 h battery and 1.43 kg, but shallower keys, dimmer screen, and slowest eligible batch time (116 s). P47 CHUWI ($1,099) ranks fourth among eligible because it nearly exhausts the budget, is 1.57 kg (only 30 g under the limit) with a 0.38 kg charger, has the shortest eligible battery (~7.6 h), and audible fans under load, despite 32 GB/1 TB, a 2560x1600 matte screen, and the fastest 50 s batch. Excluded offers are ordered below eligible per instruction: P58 (otherwise strong: 13 h, 1.18 kg, 32 GB) above P63 (disqualified by 8 GB soldered RAM).

The budget is USD 1,100 all-in. The laptop alone must weigh no more than 1.60 kg. Windows 11, at least 512 GB of storage, and no after-purchase memory upgrade are firm requirements.
I would appreciate a good display and enough memory to keep the machine useful for a few years. I do not have a fixed dollar value for these preferences. I am willing to pay more for a practical improvement, but spending the whole budget is not a goal.
I already have the required application licenses and a USB-C dock. I am not buying into a phone or tablet ecosystem and do not need a gaming GPU.
